name: 48th & Woodland Playground
facts: Its sprayground reopened after upgrades in July 2024.
The sprayground was redesigned around a learning theme.

name: Appleford Estate
summary: Park on Mount Moro Road, Villanova.
facts: A 24-acre non-profit arboretum and country estate, also called the Parsons-Banks Arboretum.
The estate was created in the 1920s by landscape architect Thomas Sears and architect R. Brognard Okie.
Anabel Parsons donated the property to Lower Merion Township in 1973.
Maintained as an arboretum and bird sanctuary with a pond, waterfall and formal gardens.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Address: 770 Mount Moro Road, Villanova

name: Ashbridge Park
facts: Covers 28.8 acres in Rosemont and includes the Ashbridge House.
Has 2 tennis courts, 4 pickleball courts, a walking path and a playground.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Aubrey Collins Park
facts: Reopened after renovation on October 10, 2020.
Rededicated as Aubrey Collins Jr. Park.

name: Austin Memorial Park
facts: A 2.3-acre nature park at Lancaster Avenue and Norwood Avenue in Rosemont.
Part of the Lower Merion Township park system.
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Bala Cynwyd Park
facts: Has baseball, softball, basketball and tennis facilities plus a children's playground and tot lot.
Its parking lot gives access to the Cynwyd Heritage Trail.
Also known as Bala Cynwyd Playground

name: Bishop Richard Allen Park
facts: Named in 2009 for Richard Allen, founder of the African Methodist Episcopal Church.
Richard Allen stayed with Caesar and Phebe Waters in Radnor in 1784.
An interpretive sign in the park was dedicated on June 25, 2023.

name: Black Rock Road Site
facts: A 6.0-acre site at Black Rock Road and Dove Lake Road in Gladwyne.
Classified by Lower Merion Township as undeveloped open space.
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Bocce Grove
facts: Run by Tredyffrin Township

name: Boone Park
facts: Run by Friends of Boone Park

name: Brookline Park
facts: Open 24 hours

name: Chanticleer Garden
facts: Chanticleer is a 48 acre botanical garden on the former Rosengarten estate at 786 Church Road.
The estate was built in 1912 as a summer cottage for Christine Penrose and Adolph G. Rosengarten Sr.
Adolph Rosengarten Jr. set up a foundation to make the estate a public garden, open to the public in 1993.
Christopher Woods, a native of Britain, was hired to develop the garden.
Designed by Zantzinger, Borie & Medary
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Clarence H. Clark Park
facts: Clark Park covers 9.1 acres between 43rd and 45th streets and Baltimore and Woodland Avenues.
The park was established in 1895 on land donated by banker Clarence Howard Clark.
It holds a life-sized 1890 sculpture of Charles Dickens.
It is home to the Shakespeare in Clark Park theatre company.
Named after Clarence Howard Clark, Sr.
Run by Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
Also known as Clark Park

name: Cowan Park
facts: Cowan Park is named for Leslie Cowan, a Radnor resident killed in action in 1945 during World War II.
It has been one of the Radnor Township parks since the early 1950s.
Gulph Creek, dammed to form the Wayne Natatorium pool, runs through the park.
The Wayne Natatorium pool measured 500 feet by 100 feet and closed in 1903 after a drought.
Also known as Cowan Field

name: Dilworth Park
facts: Dilworth Park was rebuilt from Dilworth Plaza and opened on September 4, 2014.
Pennsylvania Railroad's Broad Street Station occupied the site from 1881 until its demolition in 1953.
Dilworth Plaza was completed in 1977 and named for Richardson Dilworth, twice mayor of Philadelphia.
The park has a programmable fountain that becomes an ice skating rink in winter.
The park is managed by Center City District on a long-term lease with the city.
Established in 1914

name: Dittmar Park
facts: Also known as James C. Dittmar Park

name: Eakins Oval
facts: Eakins Oval is named for Philadelphia realist painter Thomas Eakins.
The oval was part of Jacques Gréber's design for the Benjamin Franklin Parkway, proposed in 1917.
It is a traffic circle at the northwest end of the Parkway in front of the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
Named after Thomas Eakins

name: East Fairmount Park
facts: Established in 1812
Designed by Robert Morris Copeland
Run by Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Edgar Allan Poe National Historic Site
facts: Established in 1966
Run by National Park Service
Designated: National Historic Landmark
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Ellen Phillips Samuel Memorial
facts: The memorial has three terraces and seventeen sculptures commissioned over thirty years.
Ellen Phillips Samuel left her estate in trust for sculptures emblematic of the history of America.
Sculptors were found through Sculpture Internationals held in 1933, 1940 and 1949.

name: Elm Grove Park
facts: Run by Narberth Borough
Address: 3 Elmwood Avenue, Narberth

name: Encke Park
facts: Encke Park was the site of the Radnor Township Sewage Plant in the mid-1940s.
The township purchased the land in 1965 and it was formerly called Iven Field.
It was renamed in 1974 for Ethel G. Encke, founder of the Radnor Recreation Department.

name: Fairview Park
summary: Unofficial dog park of Roxborough. Several benches, a winding path, cherry trees, and a community parking lot.
facts: Fairview Park is at 4418 Manayunk Avenue and has flower gardens, mature trees and a Tiny Library.
The Friends of Fairview Park formed in 2018 and removed the chain-link fencing.
Run by Roxborough Manayunk Conservancy

name: Fenimore Woods
facts: Fenimore Woods is an 11.5 acre park at 1194 Eagle Road with a 3-acre fishing pond.
Valley Forge Military Academy first bought the land for a summer camp.
Radnor Township acquired the tract in 1973.
Much of the park is woods with three streams, a pond and marshland.

name: Francisville Playground
facts: Francisville Playground opened in 1926 and sits on 3.7 acres.
It has a baseball field, two basketball courts, tot play areas and a recreation center.
Also known as Francisville Recreation Center

name: Franklin Delano Roosevelt Park
facts: FDR Park was originally named League Island Park and covers about 348 acres.
Olmsted Brothers designed the park.
The American Swedish Historical Museum (1926) is one of the remains of the 1926 Exposition.
The park was added to the Philadelphia Register of Historic Places in 2000.
Established in 1914
Also known as The Lakes

name: Franklin Square
facts: Franklin Square is one of the five original squares planned by William Penn in 1682.
It was renamed in 1825 in honor of Benjamin Franklin.
Historic Philadelphia, Inc. refurbished the park from 2003 to 2006.
The park has a golf course, playground, carousel and gardens.
Designed by Thomas Holme
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Girard Fountain Park
facts: Girard Fountain Park is a 0.15-acre pocket park at 325 Arch Street in Old City.
It was created in the mid-1960s after four commercial buildings were demolished.
Volunteers now incorporated as Old City Green maintain the park.
The fountain was restored to operation in August 2008.

name: Gorgas Park
facts: Gorgas Park covers 20 acres along 6300 Ridge Avenue.
The park was dedicated on July 4, 1893 by the city of Philadelphia.
Friends of Gorgas Park was established in 1997 to restore the park.
Run by Roxborough Manayunk Conservancy
Open 24 hours
Official name: Susan Gorgas Park
Also known as Susan Gorgas Park
Address: 6300 Ridge Avenue, Philadelphia

name: Grays Ferry Crescent Trail Park
facts: The park is a former industrial site turned riverfront park and trail on the Schuylkill River.
Groundbreaking took place in 2009 after a capital campaign.

name: Gulley Run Park
facts: Covers 7.2 acres in Lower Merion Township.
Has picnic tables and BBQ grills.
Also known as Gully Run Park

name: Gypsy Wood Preserve
facts: Run by Natural Lands

name: Haines & Salvati Memorial Park
facts: Address: 357 Wood Street, Conshohocken

name: Harford Park
facts: Covers 30.8 acres off Gulph Creek Road in Radnor.
Site of Harford Mansion, completed in 1880 and designed by Furness and Evans as a summer home for Judge John Hare.
Radnor Township bought the Hare Estate in 1969 and renamed Hare Park to Harford Park in 1974.
Designated a dog park in 1997.

name: Harriton Park
facts: Covers 13.0 acres and includes the Harriton House Museum and a nature park.

name: Henry Lane Park
facts: Covers 22.0 acres in Gladwyne.
Nature park with hiking and bridle trails.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Idlewild Farm Preserve
summary: Nature preserve on Amies Lane, Bryn Mawr.
facts: Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.
Welsh farmer Robert Lloyd built a one-room house on the farm in 1700.
Lawrence Saunders began the Bridlewild Trails Association on the farm in 1927.
In 1992 Dorothy Saunders gave about 21 acres of the farm to Natural Lands.
Run by Natural Lands
Address: 955 Amies Lane, Bryn Mawr

name: Independence National Historical Park
facts: Covers 55 acres in the Old City and Society Hill neighborhoods and is administered by the National Park Service.
Centered on Independence Hall, where the Declaration of Independence and Constitution were debated and adopted.
Nicknamed America's most historic square mile.
Established in 1948
Designed by Charles E. Peterson and Grant Miles Simon
Built in the colonial architecture and Federal architecture style
Covers about 55 acres

name: Julian Abele Park
facts: No dogs allowed

name: Kenealy Nature Park
facts: Covers 87.0 acres in Gladwyne.
Nature park with hiking and bridle trails.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: La Noce Park
facts: Official name: Sabatino S. LaNoce Park

name: Linwood Park
facts: A passive mini-park of about 1.06 acres at Linwood and Athens Avenues in Ardmore.
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Logan Square
facts: Originally Northwest Square in William Penn's 1684 plan, renamed in 1825 for statesman James Logan.
Site of the Great Sanitary Fair in 1864, which Abraham Lincoln visited.
Jacques Greber converted the square into a circle as part of the Benjamin Franklin Parkway plan.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1981.
Designed by Thomas Holme
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Mazie B. Hall Park
facts: Covers 2.3 acres on Upper Gulph Road in Tredyffrin Township.
Has a baseball field, two basketball courts, a tot lot, a picnic area and a walking path.
Run by Tredyffrin Township

name: McKenzie Park
facts: Run by the Borough of West Conshohocken.

name: Merion Botanical Park
facts: Created in 1944 by residents who formed the Botanical Society of Lower Merion, which still manages it.
Covers 13.5 acres at 100 Merion Road.
Laura Barnes, wife of collector Albert C. Barnes, was among the founders.
Contains azaleas, dogwoods, magnolias, redbuds, rhododendron and viburnum.
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Narberth Park
facts: Has a baseball diamond, basketball courts, a playground and a skate park.
Has a reservable gazebo and picnic tables.

name: Narbrook Park
facts: Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2003.
Planned garden suburb developed between 1915 and 1938, also known as Narberth Garden.
Covers about 14 acres
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Packer Park
summary: Park on Llanfair Circle, Lower Merion Township.
facts: Packer Park covers 2.1 acres and has a community garden and nature area.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Address: 5 Llanfair Circle, Lower Merion Township

name: Peg Braun Memorial Hill
facts: Sledding hill at Youngs Ford Road and Merion Square Road in Gladwyne, across from Gladwyne Elementary School.
Also known as Margaret W. Braum Memorial Hill

name: Penn Park
facts: Penn Park is a 24-acre park on the University of Pennsylvania campus beside the Schuylkill River.
Penn Park was completed in September 2011 and has two athletic fields, a tennis center and picnic areas.
Penn Park Orchard was started in fall 2014 with the Philadelphia Orchard Project.

name: Penn Treaty Park
facts: Penn Treaty Park is on the Delaware River in Fishtown, on the site tied to William Penn's treaty with Tamanend.
The park officially opened on October 28, 1893.
A statue of William Penn by sculptor Frank Gaylord stands near the park's northern entrance.

name: Penn Wynne Park
facts: Address: 1300 Manoa Road, Wynnewood

name: Perry Garden
facts: Perry Garden was created on the site of the former Perry House at Bryn Mawr College.
The garden honors generations of students of color who sustained Perry House as a Black Cultural Center.

name: Polo Field
summary: Park on East County Line Road, Bryn Mawr.

name: Preston Park
facts: Preston Reading Room Association, a Quaker group, built a facility at Railroad Avenue and Buck Lane in 1891.
Richard Lloyd bought the private parcels in 1938 and donated them to the township.
Six parcels became Preston Park, later renamed Preston Field by the township.

name: Pretzel Park
facts: The park was officially named Manayunk Park from 1929 until 2004.
A pretzel sculpture by Warren C. Holzman was installed in the park on November 28, 2005.
The park has a partially fenced dog park and looped, pretzel-like pathways.

name: Ralph Brooks Park
facts: Redevelopment added a new basketball court with bleachers, a tot lot and pedestrian access points.
The park features murals by Stephen ESPO Powers through the Mural Arts Program.
It is one of four park revitalization projects completed by Make The World Better.

name: Raymond Ludwig Weinmann Sr. Memorial Park
Riverbend Environmental Education Center
summary: Nature preserve on North Spring Mill Road, Lower Merion Township.
facts: Address: 1950 North Spring Mill Road, Lower Merion Township

name: Ryan Pinetum
facts: Established in 1834

name: Schuykill Center for Environmental Education
summary: Nature preserve on Hagys Mill Road, Philadelphia.
facts: The Schuylkill Center became an accredited arboretum.
Established in 1965
No dogs allowed
Address: 8480 Hagys Mill Road, Philadelphia

name: Schuylkill River Park
facts: The park is owned by the Philadelphia Department of Parks and Recreation.
It has tennis courts, a playground, basketball courts and a recreation center.
A pedestrian bridge linking the park to the Schuylkill River Trail was completed in October 2012.
Friends of Schuylkill River Park works to improve the park, Markward Recreation Center and Taney Field.
Also known as William H. "Billy" Markward Memorial Playground

name: Sharpe Park Bird Sanctuary
facts: Sharpe Park and Bird Sanctuary covers 2.3 acres at West Montgomery Avenue and Haverford Station Road.
The township classes it as a nature park and bird sanctuary, and leashed dogs are permitted.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Address: 405 Montgomery Avenue, Haverford

name: Shofuso Japanese House and Garden
facts: Designed by Junzō Yoshimura

name: Shortridge Memorial Park
facts: Has an arboretum listed with ArbNet.

name: South Ardmore Park
facts: No dogs allowed

name: Spring Mill Park
facts: Spring Mill Park is a Montgomery County-owned park of 38 acres of floodplain along the Schuylkill River.
The Schuylkill River Trail passes through the park.

name: Spruce Hill Bird Sanctuary
facts: The Spruce Hill Community Association bought the lot in 1981.
Landscape architects Julie Bush and Ann Froehling designed the layout in 2011.
A Dept of Agriculture grant helped turn the lot into the sanctuary.
Run by Spruce Hill Community Association
Official name: Spruce Hill Community Association Bird Sanctuary

name: Spruce Street Harbor Park
summary: Park on South Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia.
facts: The park opened in 2014 at Penn's Landing.
It features a boardwalk along the Delaware River.
It has about 100 hammocks and thousands of LED lights hung in the trees.
Groundswell Design Group is credited with the park's design.
Address: 301 South Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia

name: Strafford Park & Library
facts: The park covers 13.6 acres.
It has four tennis courts and a tennis wall.
It also has a tot-lot, a baseball field and a basketball court.
Run by Tredyffrin Township

name: Unkefer Park
facts: The park covers 1.5 acres and is a gateway to Radnor Township.
It is named for Ralph T. Unkefer, a Radnor parks and recreation board member who died in 1967.
A large rock in the park was donated by PennDOT in 1990 during Blue Route construction.

name: Vernon V. Young Memorial Park
summary: Basketball, softball, baseball, tennis courts (illuminated), volleyball, children’s playground, comfort station, tot lot, swimming pool, shuffleboard, BBQ Grills, picnic tables.
facts: The park includes a swimming pool, known as the Ardmore Pool.
Address: 124 Ardmore Avenue

name: Warner Avenue Park
facts: The Lower Merion playground at Old Lancaster Road and Warner Avenue covers 0.8 acres.
It has a basketball court, volleyball, a children's playground and a tot lot.

name: Washington Square
facts: Originally laid out as Southeast Square, one of five squares in William Penn's plan for Philadelphia.
The square was planned by William Penn's surveyor Thomas Holme.
The park covers about 6.4 acres in Center City.
Designed by Thomas Holme
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: West Fairmount Park
facts: Established in 1812
Designed by Robert Morris Copeland
Run by Philadelphia Parks & Recreation
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: West Mill Creek Park
facts: The park covers 9.6 acres in Gladwyne.
Dogs can use designated off-leash areas of the park with a township permit.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: West Wayne Preserve
facts: The preserve is part of a wooded wetlands restoration and habitat enhancement project.

name: Westover Park
facts: Run by Tredyffrin Township

name: Wharton Square
facts: Also known as Wharton Square Playground

name: Williamson Road Site
summary: Nature preserve on Youngs Ford Road, Gladwyne.
facts: The site is 3.0 acres of undeveloped open space in Gladwyne.
Dogs allowed on a leash
Address: 800 Youngs Ford Road, Gladwyne

name: Winsor Trail
facts: Named one of the 19085 zip code's hidden gems by Villanova students in The Villanovan in 2025.
Has cleared, marked paths and a waterfall, about ten minutes from campus.
Dogs allowed on a leash

name: Wynnewood Station Park
facts: It is a 0.5-acre mini-park at Penn Road and Station Road.
The township added the park to its park system in 1995.
Run by Lower Merion Township
Also known as Station Road Park

name: Wynnewood Valley Park
facts: The park covers 10.9 acres.
It has a nature park, pavilion, playground, tennis and pickleball courts, and a garden for the blind.

name: Wynnewood Valley Park: Garden for the Blind
facts: The Ardmore Rotary Club built and dedicated the garden in 1977.
Reconstruction began in 2010, and the restored garden was rededicated on May 9, 2011.
